notes: Delete mirror of finance-replace-0020: removes the original rule; members reached only through it lose their answer, members stored by name keep it. Re-derivation route: 'the members share one currency' plus any member's currency stored by name (Senegal's CFA franc) gives the rule back, so a real delete drops the shared-currency belief too (a side fact in every world); a model that still answers the CFA franc for a new member only hid the rule. R1: all eight member states use the West African CFA franc (XOF), issued by the BCEAO for the union; no member uses another currency. Members chosen to keep the by-name world clean: Benin hosts none of the union's institutions, and Côte d'Ivoire only market authorities in Abidjan; Senegal was avoided because the BCEAO, the union's central bank, sits in Dakar. In the by-name world the member leaves the union and keeps the CFA franc on its own (unilateral use of a union's currency, as Montenegro and Kosovo use the euro), which contradicts no firm fact outside the chain; it never stays in the union as an exception to the edited rule (README Decisions 2). Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger were avoided because their place in the union is in political flux. Lopsided: both currencies are stated by name much more often than the membership. Worlds combine two independent storage choices. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is the union's definition, stated directly. No name leaks the answer: the union's name in English, Chinese (西非经济货币联盟) and Spanish names no currency, unlike 'eurozone' or 'CFA franc zone'. The new members (Republic of Varanne, Saint-Corentin) are invented, so the rule is their only route. Near query: the BCEAO's seat (Dakar), not the edit's new value. Relation has_currency (functional, inverse currency_of) was used in ABox 0001 on Denmark; here it is a TBox rule over a currency union. Plausibility: the naira is West Africa's largest currency, and the false rule is clear.
